 News › News News › Bengaluru holiday today, November 10: Are banks, schools, colleges and offices closed for Balipadyam… Bengaluru holiday today, November 10: Are banks, schools, colleges and offices closed for Balipadyami? Check full details
 Ashita Kashyap Updated: Nov 10, 2026, 09:58 IST Bengaluru holiday today, November 10 for Balipadyami Bengaluru is observing a public holiday on November 10 for Balipadyami, also called Deepavali. The Karnataka government's 2026 holiday calendar lists the festival as a holiday while the RBI has confirmed a bank holiday in Bengaluru.
 School and college closures might depend on the announcements, from each school and each college.
 Bengaluru Holiday on November 10: What Will Remain Closed? 
 The Karnataka government's notification, issued on November 17, 2025, lists November 10, 2026 (Tuesday), as a general holiday for Balipadyami and Deepavali. The notification also states that government offices across the state will remain closed on general holidays.
 Here is what one need to know:
 1. Are banks closed in Bengaluru on November 10? 
 Yes Bank branches in Bengaluru will remain closed on Tuesday. 
 The RBI's official November 2026 holiday calendar lists November 10 as a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act.
 The holiday is listed as Diwali (Bali Pratipada), Deepawali (Govardhan Puja), Laxmi Puja and Vikram Samvat New Year Day.
 However, customers can continue using UPI, ATMs, mobile banking and internet banking services. Physical bank branches are expected to reopen on Wednesday, November 11.
 2. Are schools and colleges closed in Bengaluru? 
 Government schools and colleges are expected to observe the general holiday. 
 However, there is an important distinction in the Karnataka government's notification.
 The state has clarified that the Education Department will publish a separate holiday calendar for educational institutions. Therefore, the general holiday notification should not be treated as confirmation that every school and college, particularly private institutions, will remain closed.
 The students and parents should check the official notice issued by their respective schools and colleges before making travel or attendance plans.
 3. Are government and private offices closed? 
 All Karnataka state government offices will remain closed on November 10 for Balipadyami according to the official general holiday list.
 However, private companies, IT firms and other private establishments may follow their own holiday policies. Employees should therefore check with their respective HR departments or employers to confirm whether they have been given the day off.
 Why is Balipadyami celebrated after Diwali? 
 Balipadyami, also known as Bali Pratipada, is an important festival celebrated on the first day of the bright fortnight (Shukla Paksha) of the Hindu month of Kartika.
 The festival is associated with the story of King Mahabali and Lord Vishnu's Vamana avatar. According to Hindu tradition, Lord Vishnu sent King Mahabali to the netherworld, granting him permission to visit his people once every year.
 The day is also celebrated as Govardhan Puja and the beginning of the new year in the Vikram Samvat calendar in northern parts of India such as Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana.
 In 2026, Diwali was celebrated on Sunday, November 8, while Balipadyami falls on Tuesday, November 10. 
 While, Monday, November 9, remains a regular working day in Bengaluru.
 November 10 is an officially notified public holiday for Karnataka government offices and a confirmed bank holiday in Bengaluru. However, school, college and private office schedules should be checked through individual institutional announcements.
